result.title: Making An Actually Fun 3D Game with AI
result.description:
I vibe coded a full game sequel using Claude Code and Codex, and it proved something important about AI and game development.

A year ago I built The Librarian, a playable vibe coded game you can still find on GitHub. This time I wanted to see how far AI coding tools have come, and whether one person could build something that actually feels like a real game.

I used Claude Code with Opus 5 for the initial build, then switched to Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol for all the fine-tuning. The result is The Librarian 2, a 3D procedurally generated roguelite with boss enemies, natural disasters, meta progression, and a chaos system. 10,400 lines of code across 33 modules. Zero asset files.

The verdict: game development is far from cooked. But it's also a lot harder than the one-level demos on X make it look.

result.title: Like Slack… But for AI bots.
result.description:
Jack Dorsey’s company, Block, recently launched Buzz. It's basically a Slack workspace but for AI agents, and it's currently free, decentralized and open-source.

Here's how it works:
👋 It starts you off with a core team: Fizz (the builder), Honey (the writer), and Bumble (the researcher).
💻 You can give them parallel tasks and watch them build it in real time using any model you choose.
✍️ You can even tag them in a thread to peer-review each other's code and offer constructive feedback.
🔒 Because it's built on the open-source Nostr protocol, it's model-agnostic, decentralized, and entirely under your control.

This kind of alternative is great for developers, startups, and anyone looking to run a self-sovereign AI workforce under their own control.

Would this replace Slack for you?

result.description:
Here's how to turn AI into your own personal Jarvis 🤖

By using the voice features on ChatGPT and Claude, you can now build, edit, and iterate on interactive 3D designs in real-time—completely hands-free.

I used voice commands to generate a 3D Iron Man suit, scale the helmet, change the colors, and even add solar panels on the fly.

These voice features are currently free to use on both platforms (available on web and mobile), though paid plans will give you higher usage limits and access to smarter reasoning features.
